purpose: Trace literary and symbolic transmission of soul-pair, spiritual-affinity, fated-love, division/reunion and metaphysical relationship motifs without treating literature as doctrine.
rules: Literary evidence may establish terminology, motifs, reception and genealogy.
Literary evidence does not by itself establish doctrine or metaphysical ontology.
A literary motif cannot create an astrological rule.
Direct textual evidence is preferred to summaries.
When authorship or dating is disputed, preserve the uncertainty explicitly.

works.author: Plato
works.relevance: Major ancient antecedent for later half-soul imagery.
works.caution: The speech is a dramatic/philosophical myth within Plato's dialogue, not a modern twin-flame doctrine.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
motifs: beloved as mediator toward divine reality
works.relevance: Important Western literary example of human love becoming a vehicle for spiritual ascent and transformation.
works.caution: Beatrice should not be retrofitted automatically into soulmate, twin-flame or pre-birth-contract doctrine.

works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
motifs: conflict between social form and compelling bond
works.relevance: Influential literary metaphor for relational affinity using chemical attraction as an analogy.
works.caution: It is not a reincarnation or soul-contract doctrine.

works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
works.work: Letter to a Young Lady / later collected correspondence
works.relevance: Earliest widely cited English attestation of 'soul mate' currently identified in standard lexical histories.
works.caution: Lexical coinage does not establish split-soul or reincarnational doctrine.

works.author: Marie Corelli
direct_text_markers: half a flame that seeks the other half
works.relevance: Major documented Victorian source for exact twin-flame and twin-soul vocabulary before twentieth-century institutionalized twin-flame teachings.
works.caution: Treat as literary-esoteric transmission, not institutional doctrine; do not claim absolute first use without broader corpus proof.

works.author: Charles Mackay (traditional attribution; possible Marie Corelli collaboration)
works.work: The Twin Soul; or, The Strange Experiences of Mr. Rameses
works.relevance: Demonstrates explicit late-Victorian circulation of 'twin soul' as a literary title and motif.
works.authorship_note: Dobson and Turner (2025) argue Mackay is likely the primary author but find evidence compatible with Corelli collaboration.
works.caution: Authorship is not fully settled; literary circulation is the relevant fact.

research_queue.requirement: Use primary text plus academic commentary; separate divine-beloved mysticism from dyadic soulmate doctrine.
Treat mystical marriage primarily as soul-God relation unless a text explicitly supports another structure.
Trace terminology and reception, not doctrine by association.

targets: New Age novels and channelled literature
research_queue.requirement: Classify clearly as fiction, emic teaching or identified method.
